title.narrative: Critical and integrated assistance to unregistered refugees from South Sudan in Gambella Region’s Nuer Zone

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project, jointly implemented by Doctors with Africa CUAMM and RADO, proposes to urgently deliver crucial integrated humanitarian response to respond to the urgent needs of unregistered South Sudanese refugees and vulnerable host communities in Ethiopia’s Nuer Zone, particularly in Wantawo and Makuey Woredas. Triggered by a rapid and detailed needs assessment, the intervention will address severe gaps in health and protection services through an integrated, principled approach that prioritizes safety, dignity, and inclusion.ltbrgtThe project aims to directly support 23,329nbspSouth Sudanese refugees affected by displacement in the Gambella region, focusing on 2 pillars of intervention: (1) the health and (2) the protection componentnbsp as described below:ltbrgtIn the health sector, the project proposes to restores essential services to 2 health facilities, namely Mathar Health Centre and Nyinenyang Primary Hospital, by supplying critical medical equipment, installing solar power, and establishing a mini blood bank to ensure uninterrupted emergency and maternal care. Mobile Health and Nutrition Teams (MHNTs) will provide lifesaving services—including outpatient consultations, antenatal care, immunization, mental health support, and cholera response—to hard-to-reach areas, while ambulance support and referral mechanisms will aim to reduce delays in accessing higher-level care. Community outreach agents shall promote early detection, health awareness, and service uptake, while safeguarding and accountability will be reinforced through PSEAH training and confidential feedback mechanisms.ltbrgtCUAMM’s implementing partner, RADO, will lead the protection component, establishing community-based GBV and child protection systems, delivering case management and psychosocial support, and creating safe spaces for women, girls, and children. The project also distributes emergency shelter and kits to the most vulnerable households, with inclusive targeting and practical demonstrations to ensure safe and effective use. Dialogue sessions and joint community initiatives will promote peaceful coexistence and resilience, while a multi-channel complaint and feedback mechanism ensures transparency and community empowerment.ltbrgtThe project will benefit from the long-lasting presence of both organisations in the region and operational zones. CUAMM has worked in Gambella region of Ethiopia as one of the main health NGO partners since 2016, providing support to both host and refugee communities. Moreover, RADO and CUAMM will count on their pre-existing collaboration through the AICS-funded project INCLUSIVE “Strengthening prevention, equitable, and inclusive care for all” in Gambella (Woredas of Gabella Town, Gambella Zuria and Abobo), aimed at specifically improve the health and well-being conditions of people at risks and with disabilities in the region.ltbrgtlt/pgt
